title: Deposit by lunch or lose the room
scenario: You find a near-perfect apartment close to campus. The “landlord” says another student is ready to take it and asks for one month’s deposit by bank transfer before lunch, promising a video tour afterward.

answers.A: Do not send money before verifying the property, landlord and lease; use an in-person/verified viewing or trusted rental platform process.
answers.B: Ask the university housing office or a local contact to help verify the address and landlord before paying.
answers.C: Send a smaller holding deposit first so the landlord keeps the room while you verify.

explanation: Rental scams rely on scarcity and distance. A smaller irreversible transfer is still an irreversible transfer.
proTip: Housing pressure is real; proof of control comes before payment.
